sources.title: Saída de Jensen Huang abala Nvidia e pode redefinir o futuro da inteligência
sources.text: A renúncia de Jensen Huang ao comando da Nvidia abre uma incerteza que vai além da sucessão na fabricante de chips: a continuidade das relações comerciais e financeiras que ajudam a sustentar a expansão da inteligência artificial. O executivo tinha papel central na articulação de investimentos entre empresas do setor. A mudança ocorre em um momento em que fabricantes de semicondutores , provedores de nuvem e desenvolvedores de IA dependem de grandes compromissos financeiros para ampliar a infraestrutura necessária ao treinamento e à operação de modelos. A influência da Nvidia no mercado não se limita à venda de processadores. A empresa também participa de um ecossistema de investimentos e acordos com companhias que precisam de capacidade computacional para desenvolver serviços de inteligência artificial . Nesse arranjo, provedores de nuvem e laboratórios de IA dependem de infraestrutura equipada com chips da fabricante, enquanto os investimentos e compromissos comerciais ajudam a viabilizar novas instalações. Huang teve participação direta na construção dessas relações. Sua atuação envolvia não apenas a estratégia tecnológica da Nvidia, mas também a articulação com parceiros e clientes que impulsionam a demanda por seus produtos. A saída do executivo, portanto, levanta dúvidas sobre a capacidade da companhia de manter esse ritmo de coordenação. O desafio não está necessariamente no desenvolvimento dos próximos chips . A Nvidia conta com equipes técnicas e um planejamento de produtos que não dependem exclusivamente de seu fundador. A questão é como a empresa manterá a rede de acordos, investimentos e operações que conecta diferentes participantes do mercado de IA. Um dos pontos de atenção é o chamado financiamento circular. O modelo ocorre quando empresas que fornecem tecnologia ou infraestrutura também investem em clientes ou oferecem garantias que ajudam a financiar compras de seus próprios produtos e serviços. Esse tipo de relação pode acelerar a construção de data centers e a expansão da capacidade computacional. Ao mesmo tempo, cria vínculos financeiros entre empresas que dependem umas das outras para manter seus planos de crescimento. Se compromissos forem revistos ou novos investimentos demorarem a sair, os efeitos podem alcançar diferentes partes da cadeia. Anúncios e acordos envolvendo empresas como OpenAI , CoreWeave e Anthropic ilustram a dimensão dos recursos mobilizados para ampliar a infraestrutura de inteligência artificial. A continuidade desses projetos depende de financiamento, disponibilidade de equipamentos e confiança na demanda futura. A renúncia de Huang não significa que esses compromissos serão interrompidos. Mas sua saída acrescenta uma variável à avaliação dos investidores: quem assumirá a articulação de negócios em um setor no qual decisões de investimento de uma empresa podem influenciar os planos de várias outras? A reação inicial das ações mostrou a dimensão da preocupação dos investidores. Os papéis da Nvidia recuaram mais de 12% nas negociações iniciais desta quinta-feira (12), movimento que poderia retirar cerca de US$ 500 bilhões (aproximadamente R$ 2,78 trilhões) de seu valor de mercado. AMD e Broadcom, por outro lado, registraram altas de 2% e 5%, respectivamente. A diretora financeira Colette Kress assumirá o comando interinamente, enquanto a empresa avalia candidatos internos e externos para a sucessão definitiva. A Nvidia também terá de demonstrar que consegue preservar sua estratégia comercial e os relacionamentos construídos por Huang. O desempenho financeiro recente oferece uma base operacional robusta: a companhia reportou US$ 96,2 bilhões (cerca de R$ 533,9 bilhões) em receita no último trimestre. Ainda assim, os próximos resultados, previstos para 17 de novembro, serão acompanhados não apenas pelos números de vendas, mas também por sinais sobre demanda, entregas e novos investimentos. O alcance da transição será medido, portanto, pela capacidade da Nvidia de manter sua posição na cadeia de infraestrutura da IA. Mais do que encontrar um novo CEO, a empresa precisa mostrar que o ecossistema de negócios construído durante a gestão de Huang pode continuar funcionando sem depender de sua presença direta. Valdir Antonelli é jornalista com especialização em marketing digital e consumo.

sources.title: A divisão gamer da Nvidia pode acabar? O que acontecerá com a GeForce após renúncia de Jensen Huang
sources.text: O dia 12 de novembro de 2026 ficará marcado no mundo da tecnologia como um dos mais improváveis e até mesmo mais importantes de sua história. Nesta quinta-feira, Jensen Huang, o CEO e cofundador da Nvidia, renunciou ao cargo após um escândalo de adultério e espionagem. As reações do mercado de tecnologia e Wall Street já eram esperadas. Somente nas últimas horas, as ações da companhia verde caíram mais de 13%. O próprio Huang saiu do seleto grupo das dez pessoas mais ricas do mundo nos últimos três dias ao perder quase US$ 10 bilhões (cerca de R$ 50 bilhões) de sua fortuna absurda, estimada em mais de R$ 700 bilhões. Por mais que a indústria de tecnologia e o segmento de IA possam enfrentar um período de incertezas, a expectativa é que esse mercado continue firme. No entanto, a pergunta que uma generosa parcela do público começa a fazer é: o que acontece com os gamers de computador? Além do gigantismo em IA, a Nvidia é dona da tradicional linha de placas de vídeo GeForce, que alimenta 72% dos computadores dos gamers, segundo dados da Steam. Jogar no PC e usar uma Nvidia GeForce se tornou basicamente um sinônimo para muitos, e agora impera o medo de que essa divisão esteja ameaçada. A Nvidia publicou uma nota recente que explica a renúncia de Jensen Huang como diretor da empresa. Interinamente, Colette Kress atuará como CEO da companhia até que a empresa e o Conselho encontrem um executivo (a) definitivo. Em outras palavras, as portas da Nvidia estão abertas e não há como prever integralmente quais mudanças serão implementadas na gigante. Mesmo assim, a curto e até médio prazo talvez seja seguro dizer que a divisão GeForce de placas de vídeo ficará intocada. É verdade que a Nvidia já direcionava seus esforços quase que totalmente para o segmento corporativo, mas isso não quer dizer que a empresa abandonará seu braço de gráficos e GPUs. Arthur Igreja, especialista em tecnologia e inovação, aponta que o estágio embrionário do momento impossibilita fazer previsões assertivas . No entanto, ele explica que é improvável a Nvidia simplesmente se livrar da linha gamer, afinal de contas, ninguém parece disposto a se livrar de uma divisão inteira assim. Uma coisa é ter foco, outra, completamente diferente, é abrir mão. Essa ainda é uma linha de receita importante para a Nvidia. O especialista salienta que em momentos de crise, como o atual, a companhia precisará reunir todas as suas linhas para maximizar o lucro. O fato de a divisão GeForce existir pode até mesmo ser um fator positivo para a companhia. Aliás, a nova CEO era diretora financeira da empresa, então ela deve saber da importância dessa série e pode evitar cortes desnecessários agora. Claro, isso não significa que os produtos GeForce ficarão intocados para sempre . Um futuro CEO pode entender que a linha gamer e de itens domésticos não faz sentido e focar toda a infraestrutura da empresa para o setor corporativo. Mesmo assim, isso seria um movimento brusco extremamente arriscado. Vale notar que o mundo do hardware doméstico contempla apenas três empresas: Nvidia, AMD e Intel. A AMD é a única com força para produzir amplamente CPUs e GPUs, e a Intel engatinha no cenário das placas de vídeo. Abrir mão da série GeForce seria entregar o mercado de bandeja para a AMD e ver a Intel ganhar terreno ao longo dos anos. Arthur Igreja também aponta que o movimento de saída de Jensen Huang da Nvidia também não deve ser motivo para reduzir a crise de componentes global. “A questão da demanda é um fator externo, exógeno. Ela depende muito mais das hyperscalers e do restante do mercado, além de fatores como um eventual aumento da regulação [...] Em última instância, a NVIDIA continua sendo uma fornecedora. Ela não representa o mercado como um todo e não controla a demanda”. Mesmo com sua atuação distante do segmento gamer, Colette Kress já mostrou em algumas oportunidades que entende o fenômeno. Durante uma conversa com analistas da JPMorgan na CES 2026, a executiva foi questionada sobre a ausência de novidades para o setor na feira e respondeu que “o negócio de games tem sido um sucesso estrondoso”. Aliás, a própria entrada de Kress na Nvidia em 2013 aconteceu por conta do setor de games. Ela entrou na companhia após seus filhos recomendarem a marca por conta dos bons produtos gamer que produzia. O TecMundo já possui um ótimo conteúdo que conta detalhadamente a história completa da Nvidia, mas é sempre bom relembrar como um gigante se ergue. Tudo começou em 1993, quando Curtis Priem, Christopher Malachowski e um jovem chamado Jensen Huang fundaram a Nvidia em Sunnyvale, na Califórnia. Engana-se quem pensa que a estrada até o sucesso da Nvidia foi pavimentada com ouro - ou melhor, silício. O primeiro chip comercial da companhia surgiu apenas em 1995, o NV1, mas foi em 1997 que as coisas realmente começaram a engrenar graças ao sucesso da linha Riva. Mas foi em outubro de 1999 que a linha GeForce deu seu passo inaugural com a GeForce 256. Jensen e seus amigos acreditavam que os computadores se tornaram uma plataforma multimídia e de jogos 3D. A chegada da GeForce 256 confirmou isso ao se tornar a primeira GPU como conhecemos hoje. De 1999 até 2026 tem muita história para contar. A Nvidia comprou rivais, como a 3dfx, desenvolveu o chip do primeiro Xbox, do PlayStation 3, fez com que os usuários pudessem usar várias placas de vídeo em um único PC e por aí vai. Lá em 2008 a companhia verde resolveu lançar uma placa chamada GTX 280. A partir de então, as GTX se tornaram as placas de vídeo definitivas para os jogadores, mesmo a rival AMD tendo adquirido a fabricante de GPUs ATI para rivalizar forças. Não tinha jeito, a Nvidia dominava esse segmento. Os anos passaram e uma década depois da introdução da GTX 280 a Nvidia resolveu revolucionar o mundo dos PCs de novo: entrou em cena a linha RTX. Esses produtos, que perduram até hoje, tinham o poder para calcular raios de luz em tempo real, o Ray Tracing, e isso possibilitou que os games ficassem exponencialmente

sources.title: Trump pide a Tim Cook como CEO de NVIDIA tras la renuncia de Jensen Huang: «Una leyenda por otra leyenda»
sources.text: La renuncia de Jensen Huang como CEO de NVIDIA es, sin dudas, el tema del día . El escándalo por infidelidades le ha costado al empresario el puesto que ostentó durante los últimos 33 años , y el asunto promete seguir dando que hablar por bastante tiempo. Lo más curioso es que todos tienen una opinión sobre el tema y hasta Donald Trump ha propuesto a un reemplazante de alto perfil: Tim Cook . En las horas posteriores a la salida de Jensen Huang, Trump usó su perfil en Truth Social para postular a Cook como próximo CEO de NVIDIA. De acuerdo con el presidente de Estados Unidos, el exCEO de Apple es la única persona que tiene lo necesario para hacerse cargo de un rol tan complejo. A sabiendas de cómo piensa y actúa Donald Trump, no quedan dudas de que el mandatario estadounidense habla en serio. Claro que hoy parece improbable que Tim Cook esté dispuesto a asumir un rol tan notorio fuera de Apple, en especial por lo repentino y desastroso del desenlace de Jensen Huang. "Ahora que el CEO de NVIDIA, Jensen Huang, quien ha hecho un trabajo fantástico, ha renunciado, solo hay un hombre capaz de tomar su lugar: Tim Cook, de Apple. ¡Una leyenda reemplaza a otra leyenda! Presidente Donald J. Trump", publicó el presidente de Estados Unidos. Más allá de las virtudes de Jensen Huang y Tim Cook para conducir durante gran cantidad de años (y con gran éxito) a sus respectivas empresas, Trump no ofrece detalles de por qué el exjefe de Apple debería reemplazar a su antiguo colega en NVIDIA. Tal vez solo sea porque Cook ha sabido congraciarse con el presidente estadounidense durante sus mandatos, tal y como lo hizo Huang en su momento. Sea como sea, todavía no se sabe quién reemplazará definitivamente a Jensen Huang. Colette Kress , la jefa de finanzas de NVIDIA, fungirá de CEO interina hasta que se designe a un nuevo responsable del cargo. La junta del gigante verde anunció la puesta en marcha de un proceso de búsqueda de nuevo consejero delegado, para la cual analizará a candidatos internos y externos. Asimismo, se ha designado a Harvey C. Jones como presidente del board , el primero en ocupar ese rol en la historia de la compañía. ¿Tiene posibilidades Tim Cook de ser el próximo CEO de NVIDIA? Hasta hace menos de 15 días, era inaudito pensar en dicha empresa sin Jensen Huang como jefe, pero ya hemos visto que los imposibles no existen y que no se puede descartar nada. Dicho esto, Cook se encuentra extremadamente cómodo en su nuevo rol como presidente ejecutivo de Apple. Además, no es un directivo enfocado en producto como sí lo fue Jensen Huang ; algo que podría no importar en cualquier otra empresa, pero que ha sido crucial para el crecimiento de NVIDIA bajo el comando de un único CEO en sus 33 años de vida. Ya veremos qué novedades surgen en tal sentido.

sources.title: Who is Colette Kress? Nvidia's finance chief steps in as interim CEO after Huang exit
sources.text: Nvidia Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress, a 13-year company veteran, is taking the helm of the world's most valuable chipmaker on an interim basis after Jensen Huang's sudden resignation. "She's the only one internally that has this significant respect," Dan Ives, an analyst at Yorkville Ives & Co., told CNBC before the news had been made official. "She's more than just a CFO. I'd almost view her as more of a COO." Follow CNBC's live coverage of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation Nvidia hasn't announced a succession plan and said the board is considering internal and external candidates. Kress joined Nvidia in September 2013, after holding finance roles at Cisco , Microsoft and Texas Instruments . At Nvidia, Kress has been the other big voice on earnings calls, reporting the company's results and taking questions alongside Huang. "NVIDIA's strength has always come from its people, and together with our leadership team, I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years," Kress said in Thursday's statement . "We will continue advancing the work that has made NVIDIA a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead. Our focus remains on serving our customers, partners, developers and shareholders." Huang, who co-founded Nvidia in 1993, was known for running the company with no clear second-in-command, personally deciding which projects are a priority and emailing engineers about details. But when it came to Kress, "Jensen didn't do anything without her," Ives said. "She's a Swiss Army knife for Nvidia. Anything strategically: customers, partners, technology. She was involved." CNBC spoke to nearly a dozen Nvidia insiders and former Kress co-workers. They described her as savvy, knowledgeable, thoughtful and clear-headed. Kress is stepping in at a moment of crisis. Huang has operated as Nvidia's spokesperson, the face of the company and a founder synonymous with the brand. He also pioneered the artificial intelligence chip industry, making him the central figure in the multitrillion-dollar boom that's driving the U.S. economy. Kress "deeply understands the business and has shown fierce loyalty to the company," Daniel Newman, CEO of Futurum Group, wrote in a message to CNBC. Nvidia shares plunged 14% on Thursday after the announcement. The stock is poised for its sixth straight weekly drop, the longest slump since 2012. The shares have been dragged down by broad concerns about the AI buildout, particularly after the midterm elections, which resulted in sweeping victories for Democrats. Nvidia is scheduled to report quarterly results on Tuesday. The Huang saga burst into public view on Sunday, when the CEO apologized for being unfaithful to his wife. That followed reports that he'd had an affair with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman whom U.S. intelligence suspects is a spy. Pressure intensified late Wednesday after The New York Times reported a second affair, this one with an employee named Kimberly Powell. Kress was recognized in May as one of Fortune's most powerful women in business. Her LinkedIn profile lists her location as Saratoga, California, a wealthy city 16 miles south of Nvidia's Santa Clara headquarters. As for the long-term leadership plan, Ives said Kress will likely serve for about a year as interim CEO but the permanent replacement will come from outside the company. "You need someone that's been on the global stage," Ives said. "Given the importance of the company not just in the U.S. tech industry but the global economy." — CNBC's Seema Mody and Jordan Novet contributed to this report

sources.title: Who is Colette Kress, NVIDIA's interim CEO?
sources.text: Kress spent 25 years in various finance roles before joining NVIDIA in 2013 After 33 years as the chief executive officer of NVIDIA, Jensen Huang has resigned from the AI and gaming giant he founded . On Thursday morning, the company's board of director announced Colette Kress , NVIDIA's current executive vice president and chief financial officer, as Huang's temporary replacement. "The Board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company's operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption," newly-minted NVIDIA board chair Harvey Jones said in a release announcing Thursday's news. Kress is a relative unknown, but is taking lead of NVIDIA at tumultuous time in the company's history. Huang departure comes days after NVIDIA's board said it would investigate Huang after he admitted to having an affair with a former tech executive accused of being a Chinese intelligence asset. The New York Times later reported that Huang had also had an affair with an NVIDIA executive who reported to him. Before the revelations, the company did not have a succession plan in place. And for at least the immediate future, it's now on Kress to lead the company. Here's what we know about the executive. Kress worked at three companies before joining NVIDIA. She first spent eight years in finance roles at Texas Instruments before joining Microsoft in 1997. In 2006, six years after Steve Ballmer took over as Microsoft's CEO, she became the chief financial officer of the company's Server and Tools division. She remained with the company until 2010, when she moved to Cisco. There, she was the senior vice president and chief financial officer of the company's Business Technology and Operations Finance unit. To hear Kress tell it, Huang went out of his way to recruit her. Sometime before she joined NVIDIA in 2013, the CEO apparently sketched his vision for the company on a whiteboard. Per a 2023 interview , Huang wanted to transform NVIDIA into the dominant player in the nascent AI industry. Say what you will about Huang's personal life and judgement, the man was an AI visionary. It would be almost another four years following Kress joining NVIDIA before a group of Google researchers published " Attention Is All You Need ," the paper that introduced the world to transformer models, and nearly a decade before the release of ChatGPT. Kress partly credits her sons, who were only eight and 10 at the time, for buying Huang's pitch. Despite their young age, the two already knew of NVIDIA and its importance to gaming. In a 2024 Fortune interview , Kress said NVIDIA was the smallest company she had worked for when she joined in 2013. At the start of her tenure, NVIDIA's revenue was $4.28 billion for the year . In fiscal 2026, the company recorded a record $215.9 billion in revenue. When NVIDIA's board of directors announced Kress as Huang's temporary successor, it said it would consider both internal and external candidates to take on the role of CEO permanently, leaving the door open for her and other current NVIDIA employees to win the job. In any case, it's far too early to speculate who the company's board might interview for the job. But if you can forgive a writer a tired analogy, if Kress stays on as CEO, she is likely to be a Tim Cook-like figure, one that can stabilize the company and guide it toward continued growth. "The Board, [executive staff] and I recognize that this has been an extraordinarily difficult period and I want you to know how grateful we are for your resilience, professionalism and continued dedication," Kress wrote in her first email to NVIDIA employees after the transition was announced, according to CNBC . Still, she has a very difficult job ahead of her. Huang has agreed to testify before Congress in a hearing that the House aims to hold before the Thanksgiving holiday. The chair of the House Foreign Affairs committee, Brian Mast of Florida, said he wasn't ruling out the possibility of "public hearings for other people or other things down road." You can bet NVIDIA is likely to face an intense amount of scrutiny in the coming weeks, particularly when Democrats take control of the House and Senate at the start of next year.

stories.title: Meta’s New Agreements Bring Clean Manufacturing to Data Center Supply Chains
stories.summary: We’re bringing clean manufacturing to our data centers and setting an industry standard by entering long-term purchase agreements with low-carbon producers across our supply chain. The post Meta’s New Agreements Bring Clean Manufacturing to Data Center Supply Chains appeared first on Meta Newsroom .

sources.name: Meta Newsroom
sources.title: Meta’s New Agreements Bring Clean Manufacturing to Data Center Supply Chains
sources.text: Today, we’re sharing a new set of long-term purchase commitments spanning cement, steel, trucking, and recycled plastics. Through these commitments, we’re helping bring clean manufacturing to a commercial scale in the industries that build and supply our data centers. Building the physical infrastructure that supports Meta technologies takes significant quantities of foundation materials: cement, steel, plastics, and the freight networks that move them. Reducing the emissions associated with building infrastructure requires not only sourcing differently but bringing lower carbon materials and services into existence at commercial scale. Our multi-year commitments give suppliers the revenue certainty they need to build these solutions, and stepping in early helps demonstrate these technologies so the broader market can adopt them. These agreements build on a track record of testing, validating, and scaling lower carbon infrastructure solutions across our data center footprint. That includes piloting mass timber architecture to replace traditional carbon-intensive materials, open-sourcing AI models to design faster-curing, lower carbon concrete formulations , and joining industry peers as a founding partner of the Data Center Innovation Initiative . We’ve signed a multi-year agreement with Sublime Systems to support at least 180,000 tons of lower carbon cement production. Our support enables Sublime to build its first commercial-scale facility and gives us priority access to use Sublime Cement ® in our data center construction pipeline. We’ve also signed an agreement with lower carbon cement producer Fortera to support a new plant in Ste. Genevieve, Missouri. Both companies expect their early plants to add domestic capacity for lower carbon cement and create new American jobs. These agreements build on earlier lower carbon concrete projects with partners like CarbonBuilt and CarbiCrete . Last year, we signed a multi-year agreement to support domestic clean iron from Electra ’s first demonstration plant in Jefferson County, Colorado. We’re now taking that work from iron into steel: a new multi-year agreement with Sweden-based Stegra supports near-zero-emission primary steel, produced through a process that eliminates coal entirely from iron reduction. Structural steel reaches our data centers through global supply chains. Supporting a first-of-its-kind facility through its production ramp helps validate technologies that can scale across the global steel industry. Building on initial zero-emission freight partnerships with NFI in Virginia and Nevoya (with the Center for Green Market Activation) in Texas, we’re expanding our work with Nevoya to now include a California and Arizona route along the I-10 interstate. Electric trucks produce zero tailpipe emissions and run quieter than diesel. By supporting heavy-duty electric trucks and dedicated charging infrastructure along critical transport routes, we’re helping bring cleaner air and quieter streets along freight corridors in Virginia, Texas, California, and Arizona. The permanent, open access charging stations will support other commercial fleets along the corridor. Our long-term purchase agreement with MacroCycle Technologies is enabling the financing of their first commercial plant in the Southeastern US, which aims to divert hard-to-recycle plastic waste from landfills and local incinerators into 5,000 tons per year of high-value recycled PET. Long-term commitments to future lower carbon production help build American industrial capacity. By focusing these efforts domestically, where we are actively expanding our data center footprint, we help anchor new projects where domestic supply of clean materials and services are limited today. The benefits are tangible and local to the communities where our partners operate. Across planned and expanded US plants, this work is estimated to support hundreds of jobs across construction and long-term manufacturing. We use a range of tools to address emissions across our direct operations, energy footprint, and supply chain. Since 2020, we’ve matched 100% of our annual electricity use with clean and renewable energy, and we continuously work to reduce the emissions through efficient design, extending the life of hardware, reusing server equipment, and prioritizing recycled materials. While we work with our suppliers to use cleaner materials and services, we’re often limited by how deep into the supply chain our influence extends and what is available on the market. These long-term purchase agreements are structured to deliver Environmental Attribute Certificates (EACs), which is one way we address emissions in the most challenging sectors. With an EAC, a supplier produces verified lower carbon materials or services, Meta pays for the environmental benefit, and the material or service is used in the local market. This enables us to support lower carbon production now, and where possible, secure priority access to use these materials directly in our future data centers as new factories come online and supply chains mature. These commitments do more than secure materials and services for Meta — deploying these technologies at commercial scale helps to make them available to the entire market. That’s the outcome we are working toward: supply chains where lower carbon cement, steel, recycled plastics, and electric freight are standard options for any builder. We invite more buyers to build these markets with us. To learn more about our purchase agreements and other sustainability work, head to our sustainability website .

sources.title: US data center power demand outpaces supply by 10x
sources.text: The AI boom is facing a massive bottleneck The demand for power from the US data center boom is currently outstripping current capacity by ten times, with many developments looking for alternative sources of energy to keep their hardware online and the AI boom… booming. But with Democrats now in control of the House and Senate, the Trump administration may encounter some obstacles in continuing its attempts to turn on dirty sources of power while exempting them from environmental controls . Some AI companies have taken matters into their own hands, spinning up onsite gas turbine generators or decommissioned nuclear reactors , with a $25 billion debt on the health of Americans left to future generations to solve. The huge surge in AI demand requires billions in infrastructural investments to continue. Similar to the dot com boom where the main bottleneck was fibre cabling, the current bottleneck for AI is energy. A new report from insurance broker Howden estimates that in order to continue the current rate of data center expansion without increasing grid usage, up to 58% of power demand will need to be sourced from alternative sources. Looking at data from the US Energy Information Administration and the S&P Global since the year 2000, Howden found that data center power demand has increased by 19% year on year, while actual electricity grid expansion has only increased by 2% each year. Total grid capacity from data centers in 2025 reached 5%, whereas in 2000 it was just 0.1%. While there is significant demand on hardware for data centers — which has caused computer components such as GPUs and RAM to skyrocket — new supply chains and manufacturing is expected to ease constraints by late 2027 or early 2028. But the current growth of data center power demand could halt new data center construction by 2030, as highlighted by a Gartner report in June . Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more. Grid expansion is typically funded through ratepayers, meaning the price rises experienced by working class Americans are going towards funding new grid expansions and connections for data centers, leading experts to predict power costs in some states could rise by as much as 50% by 2030 . There are a number of alternative sources of energy that data centers are considering. Anthropic recently revealed that it is investing $3.4 billion in onsite gas turbine generators to supply the power necessary to get new sites online, but that has its own issues. In this case, Anthropic may be trading one energy crisis for another. In dodging the lack of grid capacity by turning to turbine generators, the AI company has found itself heavily reliant on natural gas supplies . The conflict in the Middle East hasn’t helped at all in this regard as other industries turn away from supply constraints placed on oil and increase their consumption of natural gas, spiking the price across the board. Gas turbine generators are not popular alternatives for those living in close proximity to data centers. Given how much power some hyperscale sites consume, some data center campuses have been equipped with ranks of gas turbine generators that emit sound levels comparable to an international airport, and the low hum has caused unexplained illnesses in local residents . Other AI companies are turning towards nuclear power to get their data centers online. Palisades Nuclear Plant in Michigan, Crane Clean Energy Center in Pennsylvania, and Duane Arnold Energy Center in Iowa are set to receive a total of $4.4 billion in federal grants to be recommissioned, with Microsoft and Google first in line to receive energy from the sites . Amazon is looking to purchase over 960 megawatts of energy from 12 small modular reactors planned to be constructed in Iowa at a cost that will likely exceed $1 billion, but the sites are yet to be approved and may not be operational until the mid-2030s. To that end, the US has just recently approved plans for the first data center-specific small nuclear reactor to provide power in Tennessee, with each modular reactor providing up to 300MW. But nuclear power is not a simple solution to the constraints placed on the US energy grid. New reactors are expensive to build, and recommissioning existing reactors requires significant investment to ensure the lifespan of a facility will meet the expected operating lifetime, with billions of dollars needed to ensure old facilities meet new and existing safety requirements. Continuing data center expansion, and the AI boom for that matter, will therefore require billions more to be invested.
